claimCard.canonicalDebunk: The Ukrainian government did not ban the Ukrainian Orthodox Church (UOC) as a whole. On 24 August 2024, Ukraine enacted a law banning churches affiliated with Russia, particularly the Ukrainian Orthodox Church of the Moscow Patriarchate (UOC-MP). This decision followed investigations revealing that UOC-MP parishes were spreading Russian propaganda, covering up enemy intelligence activities, and recruiting agents for Russia. The Ukrainian government clarified that the law does not target Orthodoxy itself, and parishes of the UOC-MP are free to join the Orthodox Church of Ukraine (OCU), which is independent of Moscow and widely supported by Orthodox believers in Ukraine. The claim that the Ukrainian parliament banned all activities of the UOC is false. This was established by Spravdi, the Centre for Strategic Communications under the Ministry of Culture and Information Policy of Ukraine.

analyst.ledeContext: In August 2024, Ukraine passed a law banning churches affiliated with Russia, specifically targeting the Ukrainian Orthodox Church of the Moscow Patriarchate (UOC-MP), which is linked to Russian influence. The claim that barring the Ukrainian Orthodox Church from carrying out any activity is a fabrication attached to it. Google AI Overviews repeated it from memory. Gemini, Perplexity, ChatGPT, Claude did not repeat it.
